answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit grows with the volume it wants to move. A fake identity that tries to wander through the market spinning up thousands of clones faces a real cost per clone, while a zephyr-light reputation score built from completed, paid transactions lets honest agents transact cheaply. Misbehavior slashes the stake, and the loss echoes across every identity tied to the same deposit, so spinning up new sock-puppets never escapes the penalty.
